original.title: Correction: NuriRoot clips long RN-web Scroll content
original.body:
### Maintenance class

Correction

### Class boundary and non-contract proof

- Broken invariant/regression being restored: `NuriRoot` uses `fill="grow"` (`flexShrink: 0`), so on React Native Web it expands to long `Screen` content instead of constraining the DS `Scroll` viewport. The `Screen` then clips overflow and account details cannot scroll.
- No intended public/observable delta: restore the already-documented `Screen` + `Header` + `Scroll` shell behavior for long content.
- Internal maintenance: not applicable.
- Bounded experiment: not applicable.

### Goal and why

Keep `NuriRoot` bounded by its host viewport so DS `Scroll` receives overflow and long web content remains reachable.

### Scope

- `packages/rn/root.tsx` root fill behavior.
- Root render test covering shrink behavior.
- React Native Web consumer verification in `nuri-com/nuri-business-app`.

### Anti-scope / non-goals

- No new prop, token, primitive, or component.
- No app-specific layout.
- No typography, color, payment, or account behavior change.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A long `Screen` + `Header` + `Scroll` tree scrolls to its end on React Native Web.
- [ ] Header remains fixed.
- [ ] Existing RN, Expo demo, type, codegen, and drift gates pass.
- [ ] `nuri-com/nuri-business-app` removes its temporary root-height host constraint after pulling the correction.

### Owning repository and base branch

`nuri-com/nuri-design-system @ main`

### Dependencies

- Consumer evidence: `nuri-com/nuri-business-app@83a87e61635f14c4edbf574eb2a066451d77e1df`

### Risk class

Product

### Authority and exclusions

Read the DS root, primitive fill mapping, root tests, and Expo demo. Change only after a human Project owner moves this item to `Ready`. Do not modify generated output, public API, or consumer business logic.

### Required verification

- Root Jest tests and full DS gates.
- RN-web runtime proof at desktop `1280x720` and mobile `390x844` showing `scrollTop === scrollHeight - clientHeight` after expanding long content.
- Downstream Business app typecheck, tests, export, and runtime scroll proof.

### Maintenance contract

- [x] This is not a Contraction, Extension, or Mixed change.
- [x] This issue/branch/PR is not Project `Ready` authorization.
- [x] The Correction has no intended public/observable delta.
- [x] Bounded Experiment rules are not applicable.
- [x] Scope, anti-scope, authority, acceptance, and verification are bounded.
- [x] Canonical issue/PR references will be used.

full_comments.body:
## Correction shipped — available as `rn/v0.1.0-alpha.14`

Merged in #214 (`9657321`) and tagged. The pin to pull is **`rn/v0.1.0-alpha.14`**.

### What changed

`NuriRoot` composed its canvas with `fill="grow"`, which resolves to `flexShrink: 0` — so the root could never be compressed below its content height. With long `Screen` content it therefore grew past the host viewport, the DS `Scroll` inherited a box as tall as its own content, and it ended up with nothing left to scroll. The overflow left the window and became unreachable, exactly as reported here.

It is now `fill="grow-shrink"` (`flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, minWidth: 0`) — an existing leaf, so **no public surface was added and no generated files changed**. The consumer-visible delta versus `alpha.13` is a single file, `packages/rn/root.tsx`.

The useful way to think about it: `Scroll` was never broken. A scroller can only scroll if something above it agreed to be bounded, and the root wasn't.

### Evidence

Measured A/B on the expo-demo web preview by restoring `flexShrink: 0` at runtime and re-measuring, in a 600px window. Done on a different screen than the one reported here, so it is an independent reproduction:

| | root | Scroll viewport | scroll range | document overflow |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 849px | 693px | **0px** | **249px outside** |
| after | 600px | 444px | **249px** | **0** |

**249 = 249** — the pixels that previously escaped the document are exactly the ones that are now scroll range. Nothing is compressed or clipped; content moves from outside the window to inside and scrollable. This also confirmed the defect was systemic rather than particular to one screen.

`grow-shrink` additionally sets `minWidth: 0`; measured as a no-op here, since the root does not sit inside a flex row.

Full RN suite green (291/291, snapshots unmoved apart from the deliberate root-test pin, which is the "root render test covering shrink behavior" this issue's scope asked for).

### Scope of the verification, stated plainly

All of the above is **React Native Web**. Native is expected to be unaffected because there the root view is sized by the system to the screen and cannot inflate the way a `div` can — but that has **not been device-verified**, and the RN tests run on `react-test-renderer`, which computes no layout. Worth a look during your next device pass.

One residual behaviour to know about: a screen taller than the window with **no** `Scroll` now clips where it previously overflowed on web. That is the intended model — `Screen + Header + Scroll` is the documented shell — and on native such a screen would have clipped before this change too.

### Your side of the acceptance criteria

Two steps left, both in `nuri-business-app`:

1. **Pull `rn/v0.1.0-alpha.14` and regenerate the vendored tree.** The unpatched documented flow should reproduce your committed tree from the pin — if you have to patch the pull script to make it work, that is an upstream problem here and we'll fix it here rather than in your repo.
2. **Remove the temporary root-height host constraint.** This is the criterion listed in the issue. If the workaround stays alongside the correction, the two mechanisms mask each other and neither is legible afterwards.

Leaving this open until that second step lands — closing it is yours once the constraint is gone and long content scrolls to its end in the app. Thanks for the precise report; the diagnosis in the issue body was exactly right.

original.body:
# Admission record — SelectTrigger (inline select trigger) + satellites

Decision-record issue per the DS-lane admission gate (agent-operating-model review §"DS lane —
split by change class"). Baseline `main@5acca9a`. Evidence: the Move boards and trigger-candidates
strip merged in #208; design session locked 2026-08-14.

## 1 · Named consumer

The Nuri app's Move flow: the From/To currency triggers inside the conversion card (operator
mock → the three boards on `packages/playground/pages/move.html`). App demand is evidence for
this decision, not automatic authorization — generality is argued separately below.

## 2 · Generality / platform invariant

- The interaction class — "press a compact labeled value to open a picker" — already exists in
  the vocabulary as SelectField (forms). The inline form of the same class recurs wherever
  selection lives inside content chrome (cards, rows, headers) rather than a form: currency,
  country, account pickers. The country picker's field is the sibling datum.
- The accessibility contract is a platform invariant the consumer cannot supply: one coupled
  press target carrying `accessibilityLabel` + `accessibilityValue` with dialog-popup semantics,
  expressed correctly on BOTH targets (web ARIA · RN role/state).
- Pressed feedback is a DS-owned convention (wash vocabulary); a consumer-composed cluster
  cannot express it (proven on the #208 boards: the composed rows are visually right and
  semantically dead).

## 3 · Abstraction trade study

- **SelectField `variant="inline"` — rejected.** SelectField's label sits OUTSIDE the pressable
  box; the inline control needs label, avatar, value, and glyph inside ONE coupled target. A
  paint variant cannot change that anatomy without weakening the hit target or changing shipped
  field behaviour. Anatomy difference ⇒ sibling element, not variant.
- **Consumer composition (status quo) — rejected** for production: no press target, wash,
  or accessibility value channel is expressible (#208 misfit log).
- **Ghost vs pill as two elements — rejected**; one element, one `variant` axis. Rendered
  side-by-side on the trigger-candidates strip; same anatomy, paint-only difference.

## 4 · Deliberately refused (anti-scope)

- Open/selection state, controllers, or group sugar — the trigger emits presses only; the
  consumer owns state (standing DS boundary).
- Row-sized targets and invisible horizontal hit slop — cluster-sized target only, with a
  documented 12px (`space.md`) clearance contract to any independent target.
- Avatar `sm` re-spec to ~30px — the sweep disproved the "unused" premise (SelectField consumes
  it internally; Move uses it; stories/tests cover it). Avatar stays 36px.
- A shared `2xl` display-typography leaf — not admitted from hypothetical long values; a
  measured parity failure with realistic maximum amounts is the only reopening condition.
- View overlap capability / seam primitive — the seam control stays consumer-owned (rank 1:
  document the composition; RN twin uses a local overlay whose parent contains the full 48×48
  target). General admission only upon an independent second consumer.
- Global glyph replacement — `caret-down` joins the set; the four `chevron-*` glyphs and the
  bare `chevron` stay untouched.

## 5 · Accepted public contract (implementation-ready) — AS ORIGINALLY DRAFTED; amended by the post-merge audit addendum below, which prevails wherever they differ

`SelectTrigger` / `nuri-select-trigger`, sibling element to SelectField.

- Parts: `Label`, `Value`, `Chevron` required; `Avatar` optional. Mechanical kebab↔Pascal names.
- Axes: `variant="ghost" | "pill"`, default `ghost`. Nothing else.
- Root behaviour only: `onPress`, `disabled`, `accessibilityLabel`, `accessibilityValue`,
  dialog-popup semantics. No open/selection state.
- Type/layout: `sm` emphasized label and value; one-line truncating value; 48px (`size.lg`)
  minimum height; full radius; cluster-sized target; no hit slop.
- Feedback: wash-only, no press scale. Ghost: transparent → `chrome.bg-subtle`. Pill: rests on
  `chrome.bg-subtle` → `chrome.bg-strong`, via an optional pressed mapping added to the
  chrome-subtle surface, consumed only by interactive nodes (static subtle surfaces
  byte-identical — asserted). Note: `chrome.bg-pressed` exists; `bg-strong` is the deliberate
  choice for the pill wash.
- Glyph: `caret-down` (new asset, intake with render check) consumed by SelectField and
  SelectTrigger chevron parts.
- Usage contract (doc, not prop): ≥ `space.md` (12px) between the trigger's press bounds and any
  independent target; compositions constrain long names rather than allow target overlap.
- Parity proof obligation: RN Move twin with adversarial long-currency/long-amount stories; the
  full swap disc responds on iOS and Android with the clearance contract held.

## Process

- Implementation brief: `prompts/brief-select-trigger-implementation.md` (coordinator-held).
- Requested: independent architect `Admit` on this issue, then the Project item flips `Ready`;
  the execution session launches only after both.

## Post-merge audit addendum (2026-08-15 · retroactive honesty)

This record was drafted before implementation but never published as an issue; the execution
session was relaunched with the gate declared satisfied. Published retroactively. The
provenance audit (operator-driven, 2026-08-14):

- The design-session "lock" this record drew on was WORKING-AGENT output from a coordinator
  brief — relayed, not ratified. Decisions standing because the OPERATOR made them against
  rendered boards: the sibling element and its anatomy; `variant="ghost" | "subtle"` with
  subtle painting like the soft Button; press scale on BOTH variants with the wash
  subtle-only; caret 18px text-coloured (SelectField keeps 24px subtle); avatar 36px;
  `3xl` amount typography.
- Agent-ranked clauses NEVER ratified: "seam control remains consumer-owned" — SUPERSEDED by
  the process model (the playground is the consumer implementation channel); the overlap
  capability goes to its own admission (see admission-bleed.md). The 12px clearance is a
  usage GUIDELINE, operator-waived for the seam composition.
- Shipped amendments recorded in PR #209: `fill: 'shrink'` (versioned add — Android measures
  flexGrow Text at full available width); `fill: 'hug'` full cross-axis semantics ratified
  post-audit, internal flag named `fitContent` (operator naming ruling).

full_comments.body:
## Architect review — verdict: **Admit**

Independent architect review (adversarial pass, repo-verified at `main@b14e5be`):

All five gate criteria are substantively present, and every checkable claim in the addendum matches the shipped descriptor (`packages/spec/components/select-trigger.ts`): `variant ghost|subtle`, press scale on both variants with the wash subtle-only, caret-down at 18px text-coloured (SelectField keeping 24px subtle), avatar sm=36px, `fill:'shrink'` on the value part with the Android flexGrow rationale, `fill:'hug'`/`fitContent`, 48px min-height, full radius, dialog-popup semantics, no state props. The anti-scope block is genuine refusal work (avatar re-spec disproven by sweep; the `2xl` typography leaf refused with a reopening condition — the token file confirms `2xl` is a reserved gap). Crucially, the record is honest that §5 as drafted is stale: the addendum names each superseded clause (pill→subtle, wash-only→scale+subtle-wash, the seam-ownership clause) and the provenance defect (agent "lock" relayed, not ratified).

Caveats, neither blocking:
1. §5 must never be cited without the addendum — the §5 heading now carries an explicit amendment pointer (applied before this review was posted).
2. Admitting this record documents, but does not bless, the process violation of launching execution with the gate declared satisfied. That lesson stands regardless of this verdict.

## Addendum 2 — operator supersessions of §5 (2026-08-15 · in-session against rendered boards)

Decision provenance: OPERATOR rulings made live against the rendered Move boards (playground + expo twin) during the coordinator session of 2026-08-15; recorded here per the admission discipline (the record precedes the merge — PR #213). Each item supersedes the corresponding §5/addendum-1 clause:

1. **Trigger min-height 48px (`size.lg`) → 36px (`size.md`).** The 48px floor made the trigger cluster dominate the card rows; ratified at 36 with the cluster-sized-target principle intact (the press target remains the painted cluster, no hit slop).
2. **Gap unified: `sm` (6px) on BOTH variants** (was ghost `xs` / subtle `sm`). The space retune (xs 4→3) had widened the ghost/subtle asymmetry to 3 vs 6; the operator ruled one gap for both.
3. **Avatar `sm` re-specced 36→24px with an 18px glyph** — deliberately REVERSING this record's anti-scope item "avatar sm stays 36px". The sweep premise behind the original refusal (sm has live consumers) still holds — every consumer moves together through the shared leaf; what changed is the operator's sizing verdict against the rendered cluster.
4. **SelectField caret 24→18px**, matching the trigger's glyph size; the SUBTLE palette deliberately kept (NOT the trigger's text-coloured caret).

Related scale ruling recorded on #212 (space `xs` 4→3px · `2xs` retired). Shipped in PR #213 commit `83229ca` with all hand-restated oracles updated deliberately.

## Architect review of Addendum 2 — verdict: **Admit-addendum**

Independent architect review (adversarial pass, repo-verified at `feat/bleed-move-reference@0699073`; PR #213 OPEN — the record precedes the merge). All four supersessions verify in the shipped spec: trigger `minHeight: 'md'` (36px) with the supersession recorded inline; `gap: 'sm'` in the shared base with no per-variant override; avatar `sm` = 24px circle + 18px glyph with the image leaf stepped down; field chevron `'xs'` with subtle kept while the trigger's caret carries no palette override. Provenance framing honest (operator rulings, record before merge).

Merge condition (non-blocking for the record): the doc IR leads still carried stale 48px/36px-avatar prose — being fixed in the same review-response series on #213 (Guard G enforces the regenerated pair).

review.title: Admission record — SelectTrigger (inline select trigger) + satellites [retroactive]
review.reason_de: SelectTrigger und die späteren Größen-/Gap-Anpassungen sind über #209/#213 im aktuellen Descriptor vorhanden; die ursprünglichen Klauseln wurden mehrfach explizit ersetzt. Eine konkrete Restabweichung bleibt: Die generierte Dokumentation verspricht Ghost-Wash, während Descriptor und Render-Test Ghost nur skalieren lassen. Dazu sind die historischen iOS-/Seam-Nachweise nicht vollständig, und der retroaktive Admission-Verstoß wird durch implementierten Code nicht geheilt.
review.next_action_de: Gemäß freigegebenem Reset zuerst vollständig archivieren, danach als NOT_PLANNED schließen; dies ist keine Erledigt-Bestätigung. Admission inklusive sämtlicher Addenda dauerhaft erhalten. Falls neu priorisiert, Ghost-Wash-Prosa im Doc-Quellmodell korrigieren und regenerieren; verbleibende iOS-/Touch-Abnahme separat nachweisen. Keine erneute Implementierung des bereits vorhandenen SelectTrigger.

original.body:
# Admission record — Bleed (controlled negative space)

Decision-record issue per the DS-lane admission gate. Prepared 2026-08-15 from the operator
design conversation (coordinator chat, not an agent session); §5 operator-ratified
2026-08-15. Baseline `main@b14e5be`.

## 1 · Named consumers (two, independent)

1. **The Move seam** — the swap disc riding the boundary between the From and To cards
   (operator mock; playground `pages/move.html` + expo-demo twin, PR #209). Today the web
   board can only approximate (flush 48px lane) and the RN twin uses a consumer-local raw
   overlay: the pattern is not expressible in vocabulary on the consumer channel.
2. **The List gutter refactor** (operator-named 2026-08-15): List currently owns its padding;
   rows should bleed past it so the pressable surface and wash run edge-to-edge while text
   stays on the gutter line. Scoped as its own follow-up brief after the Move arc.

## 2 · Generality / platform invariant

- The process model makes this structural: the playground link IS what the real consumer
  implements from — a pattern inexpressible in pure DS composition there does not exist for
  the consumer. Two independent consumers already queue for the same capability.
- The touch invariant cannot be consumer-supplied on RN: a control bleeding over siblings
  needs a containing parent for hit-testing (parent-bounds clipping — measured on device in
  the #209 arc). Only a DS element can own that on both targets.

## 3 · Abstraction trade study

- **Overlap axis on View — rejected**: implicit reference sibling; opens generic negative
  space + z-order on every composition (the escape-hatch class the DS refuses); cannot
  synthesize the containing wrapper RN hit-testing needs.
- **Dedicated `seam` element — rejected** (operator): single-purpose, coined name, not
  reusable; the seam is one instance of a general need.
- **`Bleed` element — CHOSEN**: convention-anchored (Braid Design System's Bleed; the print
  term), token-valued controlled negative space, reusable across both named consumers; the
  element IS the containing wrapper, so paint and touch invariants live inside it.

## 4 · Deliberately refused (anti-scope)

- Arbitrary/px values — edges take SPACE-scale leaves only.
- Authorable z-order — the lift is internal, fixed, non-configurable.
- Bleeding as an axis on View/stack — element only, greppable and reviewable.
- Multi-child hosting — one child; compose inside it.

## 5 · Accepted public contract (operator-ratified 2026-08-15)

`Bleed` / `nuri-bleed`:

- Attributes: `top | bottom | x | y`, each a space-scale leaf (mirroring the house padding
  suffix grammar — `paddingX`/`paddingY` — with bare names on a dedicated element; Braid's
  `horizontal|vertical` spelling deliberately not adopted). Emitted as negative margins on
  both targets.
- **No `all` shorthand, no `start`/`end` edges** (ratified): neither named consumer uses
  them; all-edge bleed is written `x` + `y`. Adding either later is a pure, non-breaking
  widening if a consumer names the need.
- One child. No other axes.
- **Lift (divergence from Braid, deliberate)**: the element paints above its siblings
  (internal z), because our consumers bleed over siblings, not only into parent padding.
  Braid bleeds into padding and needs no z promise; we do.
- **RN containment**: the container keeps its measured box while margins reposition it, so a
  bled interactive child remains fully hit-testable (the construction device-verified on
  Android in #209).
- Acceptance criteria: a bled 48px control is pressable across its full disc on web, iOS,
  and Android; static compositions without Bleed are byte-identical.
- The Move seam becomes a documented Bleed PATTERN (stack `gap="2xs"` → 4px seam; Bleed
  `top="xl" bottom="xl"` around the 48px control row → zero flow height, disc centred on the
  boundary — all token arithmetic).
- Docs: a layout-element page named "Bleed" alongside the layout primitives (mechanical
  `Bleed` ↔ `nuri-bleed`); the Move seam appears there as a pattern heading only — "seam"
  never enters API vocabulary.

## Process

- Implementation brief: to be drafted by the coordinator after operator ratification of §5.
- Sequence: this issue published with architect `Admit` → Project `Ready` → brief → one
  session (Bleed + Move reference rewrite + twin overlay retirement + doc/guards).
- The List refactor is a separate follow-up brief citing this record.

full_comments.body:
## Architect review — verdict: **Admit**

Independent architect review (adversarial pass, repo-verified at `main@b14e5be`):

The record clears all five gate criteria on the merits, prospectively this time. Two independent named consumers verified in-repo: the Move seam (the web board's commented "transparent 48px lane" approximation in `move.html`; the RN twin's consumer-local negative-margin overlay in `expo-demo/src/screens/Move.tsx`) and the List gutter (independently corroborated by `list-action.ts`'s own comment deferring "pressed bleed" to a future structure). The generality argument is structural, not hypothetical — the platform invariant (RN parent-bounds hit-testing requiring a containing wrapper) was device-verified in the #209 arc and is visible in the shipped overlay's construction. The trade study genuinely weighs three alternatives against standing DS boundaries; the anti-scope is real refusal (space-leaves only, no authorable z, no View axis, one child). The contract is implementation-ready against the existing grammar: all cited tokens exist and the pattern arithmetic is exact (`2xs` appearing twice around the zero-height row = the 4px seam; ±`xl` on a 48px row = zero flow height), matching the shipped mock's 4px `CARD_GAP`.

Conditions for the implementation brief (non-blocking for admission):
1. The doc pattern must spell out that the 4px seam derives from the stack gap appearing **twice** around the zero-height row — the one inference where a brief-deriving agent could stumble.
2. Negative-margin emission is new resolve-map surface on both targets; it is covered by the byte-identical acceptance criterion and the brief must assert it.

## Addendum — operator supersessions of §5 (2026-08-15 · in-session against rendered boards)

Decision provenance: OPERATOR rulings made live against the rendered Move boards during the coordinator session of 2026-08-15; recorded per the admission discipline (the record precedes the merge — PR #213).

1. **The seam pattern arithmetic is superseded by a space-scale retune.** §5 ratified `gap="2xs"` → 4px; implementation found `2xs` outside the layout vocabulary (`SpaceLeaf` is a deliberate 5-leaf subset — the token existed, the API leaf did not; verification gap recorded). Rather than widening the vocabulary, the operator retuned the scale: **`xs` 4→3px and `2xs` retired** (zero live consumers — legacy/archive only). The documented pattern is now: stack `gap="xs"` + Bleed `top="xl" bottom="xl"` around the 48px row → **6px seam** (the gap fires twice around the zero-flow-height row), disc centred, zero flow height. Measured on the shipped boards: seam 6.0px, disc centre delta 0.0.
2. **Contract clarification — hit transparency.** The lift promise implies the bleed band overlaps siblings; the element must therefore be TOUCH-TRANSPARENT outside its interactive content (the retired consumer overlay's `box-none` behaviour, promoted to element contract).
